decisions.reason: The exterior disk counterexample disproves the unqualified F2. Its actual uses in step 3.1 concern the bounded domains Omega and V, whose plane complements are connected and unbounded. Added unboundedness to F2 and explicitly verified it in step 3.1; the index vanishes on that complement by local constancy and its far-away value. The Statement is unchanged, and the crosscut, reflection, exterior-coordinate and uniqueness arguments remain sound under the stated AC assumption.

F4 accurately invokes the core lemma Remark, not its quadrilateral-only Statement. Core proof 1.1 establishes a.e. total differentiability via uniform coordinate quotients, slice density and openness applied to distance from the fixed A(z); core 2.1 identifies the image-area density with the absolute Jacobian and proves the lower inequality. The owning contract quotes this Remark verbatim. Checked the equivalence: analytic orientation follows by local degree and ACL; thin-strip estimates give geometric ACL, small singular-vector squares give the sharp derivative bound including rank-one exclusion, and lower area gives local L2 energy. No repair is necessary.

F2 cites the actual core Remark, which explicitly supplies a.e. total differentiability and lower area, proved in core 1.1 and 2.1; its contract quotes that Remark. Checked inverse 1.1 obtains Sobolev inverse regularity from the earlier equivalence before any area argument. Steps 2.1–3.1 use good ACL rectangle boundaries, uniform mollification, L1 determinant convergence, signed winding, Sard and countable smooth inverse branches to prove reverse area, then finite-measure uniqueness gives area equality and N for both maps. Step 4.1 uses inverse N to get a common nonsingular full-measure set before division; step 5.1 transports essential bounds. The cited interfaces are present and no repair is needed.

The rejected attribution is explicitly licensed by the inverse lemma Remark: it states area equality on relatively compact Borel sets for both f and its independently regular inverse and both null-set properties. Its complete signed-degree proof 2.1–3.1 was checked in the preceding review; the wrapper contract F2 quotes that Remark verbatim. Wrapper 5.1 therefore establishes clause (iii). Also checked its local-to-improper barrier comparison, reciprocal zero/infinite conventions and two-collar end exhaustion: neither annular bound assumes finite-ring uniformization or continuity of modulus under exhaustion. All Statement clauses are supported; no repair is necessary.

F4 explicitly cites the core Remark total-differentiability assertion, proved in core 1.1; the owning contract quotes it exactly. The qualitative bounded-H regularity input is separately and narrowly authorized in circular-metric-citation-authorization.json. Read the full local ten-page Gehring 1967 extraction: p175 assumes orientation, p176 gives ACL/L2 formulations, p179 Definition 8-prime gives qualitative bounded-H equivalence, and section 14 refers its proof elsewhere. Checked the local rank-one exclusion and singular-value argument giving sharp L; the continuum-circle modulus estimate and dyadic shrink/doubling prove the metric controls. The rejection confuses the Statement with the proved Remark; no item repair is needed.

F3 is licensed by the core Remark, whose exact text and proof 1.2 give a modulus-zero exceptional family, the AC chain rule and nonnegative Borel weighted speed. Almost every circle avoids that family: on each fixed interior polar annulus, the straight circle foliation has positive modulus for every positive-measure set of radii by Cauchy-Schwarz and polar Fubini. The contract F3 quotes the Remark accurately. Checked spherical weighted energy, short-circle separation using two avoided fixed points, equicontinuity of maps and inverses, degree preservation, weak L2 derivatives and distributional Jacobian closure with exact K. The supplied regularity suffices and no repair is necessary.

Confirmed a false Statement at allowed endpoint radii: A(1,infinity) maps to an ellipse exterior and has no second boundary ellipse, while A(0,R) has a puncture. Kept all annuli 0<=r<R<=infinity and both distortion inequalities; now states two homothetic ellipses only for finite positive radii, identifies puncture/infinity components and specifies the already-proved annular end-path convention. Step 3.1 uses the proper bi-Lipschitz affine map to transport all ends; F4 limits the finite numerical formula to 0<r<R<infinity, and the example A(1,e^{2pi}) remains unchanged. The inverse, axes, coefficients and restrictions are valid. This is a local repair, not an independent audit.
